*   **Strengths:** Provides geometrically accurate starting points, improving convergence and final reconstruction quality [S7, S8, unofficial].

The claim states that using geometrically accurate starting points (from SfM) improves convergence and final reconstruction quality. Source [S7] explicitly supports this by noting that SfM initialization provides 'geometrically accurate starting points' and results in higher PSNR (26.05 vs 20.42 for Random Init), indicating improved reconstruction quality. Source [S8] supports the aspect of convergence by stating that while random initialization eventually converges, it does so 'more slowly' compared to using SfM points, and that MVS (a denser geometric prior) is not needed because the optimizer creates detail, implying the sparse SfM points provide a sufficient and efficient geometric basis.

*   *Note:* Dense MVS clouds are discouraged as they waste time and bake in MVS errors [S8, unofficial].

The claim states that dense MVS clouds are discouraged because they waste time and bake in MVS errors. Source [S8] explicitly states: 'Running MVS before splatting is mostly wasted time and, worse, MVS points carry their own errors that you would be baking in as a starting bias.' It further notes that 'Gaussian Splatting does not need the dense cloud' and that initialization is done directly from sparse SfM points. Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.

It sets itself apart from dense MVS initialization by avoiding the baking of MVS errors and redundant geometry, relying instead on the optimizer to create detail during training [S8, unofficial].

The claim states that the method avoids baking MVS errors and redundant geometry by relying on the optimizer to create detail during training, rather than using dense MVS initialization. Source [S8] explicitly supports this by stating: 1) 'Gaussian Splatting does not need the dense cloud' and initializes directly from sparse SfM points. 2) 'Running MVS before splatting is mostly wasted time and, worse, MVS points carry their own errors that you would be baking in as a starting bias.' 3) 'The optimization creates its own detail as it runs, as we will see, so it does not depend on MVS to hand it a dense starting geometry.' All facts in the claim are present in the evidence.
